subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi was a Keeper of the Tome who was murdered after being struck in the face, falling forward and chipping a tooth, and then having his heart torn out and his ribcage smashed, with blackened finger and lip indicating he had been reading a poisoned page and wetting his fingertip on his lip.
source_quote: Janussi, Keeper of the Tome, was laid out before us, and the early findings were already on the table. The heart was gone — torn out, not for any wound it would cause, but as a guard against any working that calls the dead back to answer. The tip of his left forefinger was blackened. Not blue. Darker than blue. And the same dark smudge sat dead-center on his lower lip.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi had been taking notes in blue ink at the time of his death, with fresh stains on his right sleeve — the working hand — and a chip in one front tooth from a forward fall.
source_quote: Clotted blood under the nose. Smeared bloodstains on the right sleeve of the tunic — the *right* sleeve, the working hand. And blotches of midnight blue across the cuff. I knew that blue. 'Wasn't the blue ink — the ink they used in the books?' It was. Janussi had been taking notes when this happened. Writing hand, fresh stains. A man interrupted at work. And a chip in one of his front teeth, the edge jagged. Recent.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi’s tongue was blackened at the tip, confirming ingestion of the black substance, and his nose was broken before death, as bruising cannot form on a corpse.
source_quote: The tongue, blackened at the tip — ingestion confirmed twice over now. And a chip in one of his front teeth, the edge jagged. Recent. Not an old break worn smooth, but a fresh wound. The bruising around the broken nose held its color, dark and settled, the way bruising only sits when blood was still moving when it formed. My focus narrowed and held, and the picture came clear and certain: this happened before he died.

subject: Keeper's Chamber
fact: The Keeper's Chamber contained a silver pedestal, an ebony pipe with cherry tobacco, an open safe with scattered empty pouches, loose sapphires, and scraps of parchment naming spells, with four sealed pouches, a figurine of a raven, a potion of supreme healing, a potion of water breathing, five diamonds, platinum, and gold left untouched.
source_quote: The safe. A box of metal as wide as a man's reach, sunk into the tower wall, its door standing open. Empty pouches scattered in front of it, sapphires loose and dazzling, scraps of parchment naming spells. But still inside the safe were four sealed pouches, each with its sapphire — and beside them a figurine of a raven, a potion of supreme healing, another of water breathing, five diamonds each worth a fortune, a heap of platinum and gold, a small treasury left untouched.

subject: Keeper's Chamber
fact: The Keeper's Chamber held an armchair with three circular impacts and two holes punched clean through the back, indicating darts of pure force had been fired at it, not at the body.
source_quote: Daz drifted to the armchair next, and read the wounds in it the way he'd read the wounds in the man. Three circular impacts, horsehair stuffing scattered, two holes punched clean through the chair back. He studied it and pronounced it: darts of pure force. Somebody had been furious. But not at the keeper — those darts never miss their mark, Thorin pointed out, and the man bore no such marks. Somebody had aimed three bolts of force at a chair.

subject: Keeper's Chamber
fact: A three-foot marble statue of the hooded bearded old man holding a candle aloft — the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore — was toppled near the armchairs and tea table, having been knocked over in shock upon discovering the body.
source_quote: Last, the statue. Three feet of marble, a hooded bearded old man holding a candle aloft, toppled on the floor near the armchairs and the tea table. The statue had simply fallen, it turned out. The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.

subject: the black substance
fact: The black substance found on Janussi’s finger, lip, and tongue was not ink, not poison from his inkwell, and was unidentifiable even by Glabbagool, an ooze that has ingested the Underdark — indicating it was something uniquely dangerous and unnatural.
source_quote: Darkness than blue. That was the entire point of the long look — not that the finger was stained, but that the stain was *wrong*. Darker than anything in his inkwell. Zalthir, ever the auditor of other people's competence, pushed on it — *our great detective took his long, careful look and still can't tell us if it's ink?* No. That was exactly what I could tell. The skill wasn't in identifying the substance. It was in knowing, with certainty, what it was *not*. Would't Glabbagool have ingested, like, all sorts of different kinds of materials and poisons and goo in the Underdark? We gave him the substance. He gave it his best. It wasn't enough — a thin first effort, then a second pass with help, and still nothing he could name. But even his failure carried a verdict: there was *something* about the black, something that mattered.

subject: the locket
fact: A locket or necklace was torn from Janussi’s neck, leaving broken lead links and worn impressions where it had hung, suggesting it was a personal, long-carried item of significance.
source_quote: The neck told us more. The impression of a chain on the back and sides, and beneath it two broken lead links. Something had hung there, and someone had torn it off him. A locket, a necklace — gone, snapped at the chain. I have catalogued a great many sacred spaces in my time, and there is a particular grief in an empty setting where something belonged. The links were worn where it had hung. Whatever it was, he'd carried it a long time.

subject: the missing sapphire
fact: One sapphire was missing from the safe, while four others remained sealed in pouches, indicating the thief sought not treasure but a specific component for a spell requiring a single sapphire.
source_quote: But one sapphire was missing. One parchment. 'Somebody is trying to build a sapphire spell,' he said, 'a spell that requires a sapphire.' And here is where the room stopped making sense as a robbery. Because still inside the safe were four sealed pouches, each with its sapphire — and beside them a figurine of a raven, a potion of supreme healing, another of water breathing, five diamonds each worth a fortune, a heap of platinum and gold, a small treasury left untouched.

subject: The Discoveries
fact: The spellbook *The Discoveries* was the last thing Janussi wrote in, with fresh blue ink noting unfamiliar spells, and its entries were newer than those in *The Golden Ass*, confirming it was his final act before death.
source_quote: In the middle of the desk sat a spellbook. *The Discoveries.* Beside it, blue ink, fresh enough that it had a sequence to it. There was more than one color on those pages, and I wanted the newest one isolated before anything else. The blue ink on *The Discoveries* had been laid down after the blue ink on another book. *The Golden Ass.* 'So that's the last thing he was writing?' Confirmation. The spell research was the final thing under his hand.

subject: Janussi's death sequence
fact: Janussi was assaulted before death — struck in the face, breaking his nose — then returned to his desk, wrote in *The Discoveries*, read a poisoned page, wetted his fingertip on his lip, fell forward, chipping his tooth, and was later found and desecrated by a deliberate, unhurried killer who removed his heart and took one sapphire and a locket.
source_quote: A man at his books, wetting his finger to turn a poisoned page. The black climbing through him while he read on, suspecting nothing. A fall, forward, hard — a broken nose, a chipped tooth on the stone. And then the patient hands arriving after, in no hurry at all, rolling the body and opening the chest to make certain he stayed gone.

subject: the attack on the armchair
fact: Three darts of pure force were fired at the armchair in the Keeper's Chamber, missing Janussi entirely, suggesting the attacker was enraged but not targeting the Keeper directly at that moment.
source_quote: Three circular impacts, horsehair stuffing scattered, two holes punched clean through the chair back. He studied it and pronounced it: darts of pure force. Somebody had been furious. But not at the keeper — those darts never miss their mark, Thorin pointed out, and the man bore no such marks. Somebody had aimed three bolts of force at a chair.

subject: the discovery of the body
fact: The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore discovered the body at dawn and knocked over the marble statue of himself in shock, an accidental disruption to the scene.
source_quote: The statue had simply fallen, it turned out. The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.

subject: the theft from the safe
fact: The safe was opened without force, and only one sapphire and one parchment were taken, while a vast treasure remained untouched, indicating the thief had a precise, non-greedy objective.
source_quote: The killer had the combination, or had no need of one. In other words, score what they left them. A small fortune, untouched. Whoever did this came in, took one sapphire, and walked past a king's ransom.

subject: Glabbagool's failed analysis
fact: Glabbagool, an ooze that has consumed the Underdark, could not identify the black substance on Janussi’s body, confirming it was an unknown and exceptionally dangerous material.
source_quote: We gave him the substance. He gave it his best. It wasn't enough — a thin first effort, then a second pass with help, and still nothing he could name. But even his failure carried a verdict: there was *something* about the black, something that mattered. When even a creature that has eaten the Underdark can't place a poison, you've learned the poison is worth being afraid of.

subject: Keeper's Desk
fact: The Keeper's Desk held blue ink, *The Discoveries*, *The Golden Ass*, and other writing materials, with the blue ink in *The Discoveries* being the most recent, indicating Janussi’s final intellectual activity before death.
source_quote: In the middle of the desk sat a spellbook. *The Discoveries.* Beside it, blue ink, fresh enough that it had a sequence to it. The blue ink on *The Discoveries* had been laid down after the blue ink on another book. *The Golden Ass.*

subject: the ebony pipe with cherry tobacco
fact: An ebony pipe with cherry tobacco was found on the desk, suggesting the killer may have used smoke to mask the odor of poison.
source_quote: A silver pedestal by the desk, an ebony pipe finely carved, cherry tobacco. Pretty, until Zalthir's instinct landed it — tobacco smoke would hide the smell of poison. Of course it would.

subject: the interrogation of the statue
fact: Thorin expressed fear that the statue of the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore might awaken, causing Tadric to become unnerved, though the statue had merely been knocked over accidentally.
source_quote: 'Shake the candle,' Thorin said. 'I don't want it to wake up and attack us,' Thorin explained. 'I've had, you know, had bad experiences.' It worked on poor Tadric exactly as you'd fear. He tried not to look at the candle and then could not stop looking at the candle, and finally turned to Thorin. 'Are you sure this — is it true about candles?'

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced by the continuing speaker banner as the POV character who observes the ink and parchment clues, and who accepts herbal tea from Hollypocket with unusual enthusiasm.
source_quote: [Continuing — Speaker: Zalthir, Scene: Clues in the Ink and Parchment]

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is the one who says, 'have any enemies, right?' and later proposes finding the housekeeper to determine what is missing or out of place.
source_quote: have any enemies, right?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin asks, 'Wait, is that describing the type of writing?' and identifies the gift tag's script as 'grumpy' and 'cramped,' and later says, 'Okay, so yeah, there's definitely some sort of poison going on,' and 'Am I reaching too deep here?'
source_quote: Wait, is that describing the type of writing?

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the one who says, 'I like the way you're thinking,' and later listens intently when Hollypocket describes Sylvira Savikas carrying a lantern, and is noted as paying no attention to her weeping.
source_quote: I like the way you're thinking,

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris identifies Daral Yashenti as Janussi’s long-time rival and reveals that Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library, and that the other key is held by Kalan.
source_quote: Oh, that'll be Daral Yashenti. Those two have been at each other's throats for years.

subject: Hollypocket
fact: Hollypocket reports overhearing violent arguments between Janussi and Kalan Strongbranch, Teles Ahvoste, Daral Yashenti, and Sylvira Savikas, and describes seeing Sylvira's face glowing red in candlelight at 2–3 a.m. while carrying a lantern.
source_quote: I was bringing the keeper his morning tea when I passed Kalan Strongbranch on the steps.

subject: Daral Yashenti
fact: Daral Yashenti is described as having shouted at Janussi, 'You're not fit to be the candle keep's keeper,' and called him 'nothing but a glorified book peddler,' and was heard pounding on Janussi’s door at half past ten, leading to a loud argument before fleeing.
source_quote: You're not fit to be the candle keep's keeper, Daral shouted at poor Janussi

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas is described as screaming that Janussi was a traitor, nearly taking the door off its hinges, and was seen by Hollypocket at 2–3 a.m. with a glowing red face and carrying a lantern despite being a tiefling who can see in the dark.
source_quote: That devil woman! She gives me the heebie-jeebies!

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is described by Hollypocket as having a face like thunder when passing her on the steps, and is identified by Fembris as the keeper of the second key to the Hightower Library.
source_quote: I was bringing the keeper his morning tea when I passed Kalan Strongbranch on the steps.

subject: Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste is reported by Hollypocket to have shouted 'hypocrite' at Janussi during a meeting around the ninth bell.
source_quote: I did hear Teles shout, *hypocrite*, at poor Janussi before he stormed out.

subject: Hightower Library
fact: The Hightower Library is referenced as having two keys — one held by the dead Janussi and one held by the gate warden Kalan — and is implied to have had materials deleted or tampered with.
source_quote: Janussi held one of the two keys of the, of the Hightower Library.

subject: locket
fact: The locket is described as having been worn by Janussi always, never taken off, and now missing from his neck.
source_quote: the locket was missing. Off Janussi's neck.

subject: gift tag
fact: The gift tag is described as being written in a cramped, sour hand with the message: 'To Janussi, read it and weep, you old snob, a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival.'
source_quote: To Janussi, read it and weep, you old snob, a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival.

subject: lantern
fact: The lantern is noted as being carried by Sylvira Savikas at 2–3 a.m., despite her being a tiefling who can see in the dark without light, indicating its use was to conceal something.
source_quote: she was carrying a lantern. She's a tiefling, and she can see in the dark without any light at all.

subject: black residue
fact: The black residue is described as being on Janussi’s fingers and mouth, definitively not from the blue ink, and associated with poison.
source_quote: Black. Definitively not the blue ink — Grygum had already settled that, checked it twice and certain.

subject: blue ink
fact: The blue ink is described as capturing both notes on obscure spells and jokes, written in the same hand, with the joke annotations dried first.
source_quote: The blue ink captures both notes on obscure spells and jokes?

subject: Garden Shadow
fact: The Garden Shadow is referenced as having a saying about absence — 'a room tells you most by what it is missing' — though it is unclear whether the saying belongs to the place or to Brother Tharusk.
source_quote: The Garden Shadow had a saying about that — or possibly Brother Tharusk did, the tall one who always smelled of incense

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is referenced as a place with fine books but a toxic culture of scholars who hoard grudges like dragons hoard gold.
source_quote: I despise this whole place a little — not Candlekeep, Candlekeep's fine, the books are fine — but the *culture* of it

subject: midnight thud
fact: The midnight thud is reported by Hollypocket as a sound heard upstairs after the bell tower rang, which she later realized may have been the moment Janussi died.
source_quote: I thought I heard a thud upstairs.

subject: Janussi's final meetings
fact: Janussi held a series of one-on-one meetings with the Great Readers the morning of his death, each ending in explosive shouting matches with Kalan, Teles, Daral, and Sylvira.
source_quote: Janussi had spent his last morning in a series of one-on-one meetings with the Great Readers, clearing business before Deadwinter Day.

subject: Daral's second visit
fact: Daral Yashenti returned to Janussi’s chamber at half past ten, drunk, pounded on the door, argued loudly, and then fled down the stairs — the first time Janussi was seen running away from someone.
source_quote: Daral came back at half past ten, drunk as a skunk, pounding on the door until Janussi let him in, another loud argument, then the slam and the great reader running back down the stairs.

subject: Sylvira's nocturnal appearance
fact: Sylvira Savikas was seen by Hollypocket at 2–3 a.m. with her face glowing red in candlelight, carrying a lantern she had no need for, then vanishing.
source_quote: I swear I could see that devil woman's — Sylvira Savikas's — face glowing red in the candlelight.

subject: Keeper's tower
fact: The Keeper's tower is referenced as the location of Hollypocket’s apartment below it, and the site of Janussi’s chamber and death.
source_quote: Hollypocket's apartment sat below the Keeper's tower

subject: Stonespeaker crystal
fact: The Stonespeaker crystal is described as granting Daz the ability to talk to beasts, and was used to initiate the cat interrogation.
source_quote: Talking to beasts, yeah. It's part of what the stone speaker crystal grants me.

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi is described as a scholar who kept his chamber thick with tobacco smoke to medicate his failing lungs, annotated a comedy book with both jokes and spell notes in blue ink, carried a locket always, and was the target of multiple violent arguments.
source_quote: Janussi had loved the stuff — kept his chamber thick with it, medicated his failing lungs with the smell of it, lived inside a haze on purpose.

subject: Underdark
fact: The Underdark is referenced by Zalthir as a place where violence is honest and six angles are run at once, contrasted with Candlekeep’s hidden grudges.
source_quote: In the Underdark everyone runs six angles at once and at least there it's honest about being a knife fight.

subject: the missing book
fact: The missing book — *The Golden Ass* — is described as having been annotated by Janussi with jokes and spell notes, then walked out of the room, and is suspected of containing a cipher or replacement code.
source_quote: The Golden Ass was a comedy. Janussi had been writing down jokes he found funny — the man had a sense of humor he'd evidently kept private.

subject: the poison theory
fact: The poison theory is proposed as the reason the smoke in Janussi’s chamber was used — not to kill, but to mask the smell of poison, and the black residue on his mouth supports this.
source_quote: The one thing that tobacco smoke would do is hide the smell of poison.

subject: the cipher theory
fact: The cipher theory is proposed by Thorin — that Janussi used *The Golden Ass* as a key to a replacement cipher, and the book’s absence prevents decryption.
source_quote: There's something written in the book that wasn't part of the original book — or maybe he's using the book and the notes to do some sort of cipher.

subject: Brother Tharusk
fact: Brother Tharusk is referenced as possibly the originator of the Garden Shadow’s saying about absence, described as the tall one who always smelled of incense.
source_quote: The Garden Shadow had a saying about that — or possibly Brother Tharusk did, the tall one who always smelled of incense

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan is identified as the gate warden who holds the second key to the Hightower Library, and is described by Hollypocket as having a face like thunder when seen on the steps.
source_quote: that the other key is heralded by the gate warden, Kalan.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is relieved that someone else has taken an expense off his account, saving him money on potions.
source_quote: Well, that saves me money on potions," said Grygum, relieved — someone else had just taken an expense off his account.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie introduces herself as a five-year-old, sleet-grey cat entirely uninterested in being disturbed, and announces, 'I did not order any more ticklers!'
source_quote: The cat introduced herself, after a fashion. Queenie — five years old, sleet-grey, and entirely uninterested in being disturbed. "I did not order any more ticklers!" she announced, stretching.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz says, 'I'll give Queenie a little tickle,' and tickles her, acknowledging that information is currency and so is scratching behind the ears.
source_quote: "I'll give Queenie a little tickle," I said, and tickled. Information is currency. So, evidently, is scratching behind the ears.

subject: Janussi's armchair
fact: Janussi's armchair is where Queenie had settled for a nap, only to be rudely awakened thirty minutes later by Sylvira Savikas blasting the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light.
source_quote: She had settled into Janussi's armchair for a nap, she said, "only to be rudely awakened some thirty minutes later by our Sylvira Savikas, this is in the morning, blasting the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light."

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas is a tiefling who blasted the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light, waking Queenie from her nap.
source_quote: Sylvira Savikas, this is in the morning, blasting the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin asks, 'what was going on with those bolts of force, do we know why,' and later notes that the victim was still alive when Daral left.
source_quote: Thorin dug in — *what was going on with those bolts of force, do we know why* — and the answer arrived dressed as gossip: Sylvira the tiefling, and Janussi, an on-and-off-again relationship.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin identifies a 'shapeshifter situation' after Queenie describes a figure wearing Sylvira's shape but not her scent.
source_quote: "Oh, so we've got, like, a shapeshifter situation going on here," said Thorin.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir says, 'That explains the candle,' after Thorin identifies the shapeshifter situation, and later incorrectly identifies the book as a TV.
source_quote: "That explains the candle," said Zalthir, and the picture began to assemble itself.

subject: The Golden Ass
fact: The Golden Ass is a dull book that holds a person motionless and uninterested in scratching a cat, and was taken from the room under Daral's arm.
source_quote: "Every time they open that block," Queenie said, "they just sit there and don't tickle!" A book. Not a device, not an enchantment — a book, dull enough to hold a person motionless and uninterested in scratching a cat. *The Golden Ass*, the missing volume, walking out of the room under Daral's arm.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral is described as the 'stinky breath one' by Queenie, and is the one who carried away The Golden Ass under his arm.
source_quote: there is a precision to how cats categorize people that I find I respect. No titles. No politics. Just the relevant data: gait, smell. ... and later Daral, *the stinky breath one*.

subject: corridor
fact: Queenie retreated to the corridor after Daral shouted too much, and later saw him run downstairs with a hypnotic block.
source_quote: she retreated to the corridor — "when I later saw him run downstairs with a hypnotic block."

subject: Fheminor
fact: Fheminor is described by Queenie as 'the short-legged one' and is the first evening guest to arrive.
source_quote: first Fheminor, *the short-legged one*, and later Daral, *the stinky breath one*.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie describes a figure wearing Sylvira's shape but not her scent, calling her 'the torn demon lady' but noting, 'she didn't smell like the demon lady, though.'
source_quote: She'd prowled the nighttime cycle and seen *the torn demon lady* coming down the steps — Sylvira's shape — "But she didn't smell like the demon lady, though."

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie says, 'There have been too little Tickles and too many questions,' and refuses to be more generous until more tickles are given.
source_quote: "There have been too little Tickles and too many questions." I tickled. I tickled some more.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie assesses two-leggers as never licking themselves, and claims to have met cleaner dogs in her time.
source_quote: How would I know? I try to hold my breath whenever a two-legger passes. It's clear that you hardly ever lick yourselves at all. I've met cleaner dogs in my time.

subject: the locket
fact: The locket is described by Queenie as intimate, carried all the time, never taken off, but its nature is unknown to her.
source_quote: The locket itself is intimate. He carried it all the time. He never took it off." "I don't know what it was.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris supplies the missing detail that Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library.
source_quote: Fembris, *by golly*, supplied the column I was missing: Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan is the gate warden who holds the other key to the Hightower Library.
source_quote: The other key, I learned, rested with Kalan, the gate warden.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie tells Daz to leave and to give himself a proper licking before returning to her tower.
source_quote: "You may now leave," she said, "and please give yourself a proper licking before returning to my tower."
